title: Mokuʻula restoration master plan
summary: At the August 6 meeting, a commissioner said they were very supportive of the restoration project, and the commission took no action. The department's first step is removing the courts and parking lot, with archaeological and cultural monitors on all work and topsoil placed over cleared areas. It is working with the Salvation Army to acquire land the group still owns, and the master plan, being developed until June 2027, will build in the commission's 2019 recommendations.

timeline.text: Maui Now published an update on Mayor Bissen's and the Department of ʻŌiwi Resources' plans to restore Mokuʻula and Loko o Mokuhinia after ancestral waterways resurfaced following the 2023 wildfires.

source.quote: Mokuʻula and Loko o Mokuhinia are sacred places with deep cultural and historical significance, and their restoration represents an opportunity to reconnect with that part of our history while helping guide Lahaina's future.

timeline.text: Maui Daily reported that county officials call the surface-clearing work 'Phase Zero' and expect it to begin in the coming weeks, under archaeological and cultural monitoring.

source.quote: preparatory work at Lahina's historic Moola site is expected to begin in the coming weeks with crews removing former tennis courts a basketball court and a parking lot to prepare the area for long-term restoration county officials say the work is considered phase zero and will be monitored by archaeologists and cultural practitioners.
